info.title: TextKit - Sentiment, Language, Readability & Keywords
info.description:
# TextKit: Sentiment, Language, Readability and Keywords

Fast, deterministic natural-language utilities: sentiment, language detection, readability grades, keywords, extractive summaries, profanity masking, slugs and text statistics. No LLM involved, so results are instant, cheap and repeatable.

**Who it's for:** product teams analysing reviews and support tickets, content and SEO tools, moderation pipelines, CMSs and edtech.

## Use cases
- Tag customer reviews and tickets as positive or negative and route the angry ones first.
- Detect a message's language before translation or routing.
- Enforce a target reading grade for help-centre or public-sector content.
- Auto-generate tags, SEO keywords and slugs when publishing articles.
- Mask profanity in usernames, comments and chat.

## Quickstart
Subscribe on RapidAPI (a free plan is available), copy your key, then:

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://textkit-sentiment-language-readability-keywords.p.rapidapi.com/sentiment?text=I%20love%20this%20product%20but%20shipping%20was%20slow.' \
  --header 'X-RapidAPI-Key: YOUR_RAPIDAPI_KEY' \
  --header 'X-RapidAPI-Host: textkit-sentiment-language-readability-keywords.p.rapidapi.com'
```

## Authentication
Every request goes through RapidAPI. Send `X-RapidAPI-Key` (your key) and `X-RapidAPI-Host` (`textkit-sentiment-language-readability-keywords.p.rapidapi.com`) on every call. Requests that bypass the gateway are rejected with `403`.

## Good to know
- Input limit is 50,000 characters per request (`413` above that).
- Sentiment, readability, keywords, profanity and summaries are tuned for English; language detection covers 55 languages.
- All results are deterministic: the same text always gives the same output.

## Rate limits and plans
Request quotas and per-second limits depend on the RapidAPI plan you subscribe to; see the Pricing tab. When a limit is reached the gateway returns `429 Too Many Requests`; retry with exponential backoff or move to a higher plan.

## Errors
All errors are JSON. The API returns `{"error": "<reason>"}` with a meaningful HTTP status: `413` input too large, `422` missing or invalid parameter. Gateway errors (`401`/`403`/`429`) come from RapidAPI as `{"message": "<reason>"}`.

## Data sources and licences
- Sentiment: VADER (Hutto and Gilbert, 2014), MIT licence.
- Language detection: langdetect, a port of Google's language-detection library, Apache 2.0 licence.
- Readability formulas: Flesch, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Coleman-Liau and ARI (public formulas).

## MCP (AI agents)
This API is also available as a Model Context Protocol server at `POST /mcp` on the same RapidAPI host; see the MCP endpoint for setup.

get.summary: Run every analysis in one call
get.description: Returns statistics, sentiment (without per-sentence detail), top 10 keywords, language and readability in a single response. One request instead of five.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: I love this product but shipping was slow.

get.description: Scores sentiment with VADER, a lexicon and rule-based model tuned for reviews and social media (handles emphasis, negation, emoji and slang). Returns a label, a -1..+1 compound score, positive/neutral/negative proportions and per-sentence scores. Best for English.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: I love this product. But shipping was slow and the box was damaged.

sentences.text: But shipping was slow and the box was damaged.

get.description: Identifies the language among 55 supported (ISO 639-1 codes) with a probability, plus up to 5 candidates. Accuracy improves with longer text; very short or letter-free text returns 422.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: Bonjour tout le monde, comment allez-vous ?

422.description: Missing text, or language could not be detected.

example.error: Could not detect language (text too short or no letters)

get.description: Computes Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid grade, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Coleman-Liau and ARI, a consensus grade, a plain-English level and reading time. Designed for English prose.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: Bristol is a city in south west England with a population of around 470,000. It sits on the River Avon and has a long maritime history. The city is known for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel.

get.description: Finds the most relevant single words (stop words removed, scored by frequency and length) and the most frequent multi-word phrases. Useful for tagging, SEO and search indexing. English stop-word list.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: Bristol is a city in south west England with a population of around 470,000. It sits on the River Avon and has a long maritime history. The city is known for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Number of keywords and phrases to return (clamped to 1-50).

get.description: Selects the most informative sentences (word-frequency scoring with a lead-sentence bonus) and returns them in original order. Sentences of 20 characters or fewer are ignored. Deterministic and fast; no generative model, so nothing is invented.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: Bristol is a city in south west England with a population of around 470,000. It sits on the River Avon and has a long maritime history. The city is known for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel.

parameters.name: sentences
parameters.description: Number of sentences in the summary (clamped to 1-20).

example.summary: Bristol is a city in south west England with a population of around 470,000. The city is known for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel.

get.description: Detects English swear words and simple variants (for example plural or -ing forms) and returns a censored copy where each letter is replaced by the mask character.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.
parameters.example: What the hell, this is bullshit

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Masking character (only the first character is used).

get.summary: Convert text to a URL slug
get.description: Transliterates accents to ASCII, lower-cases, and joins words with the separator to create a clean URL slug (max 200 characters).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Text to analyse (UTF-8, max 50,000 characters; longer text returns 413). Long text in a query string is subject to URL length limits of your HTTP client, so keep GET requests to a few KB.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: Word separator: `-` or `_`. Anything else falls back to `-`.

get.summary: Count words, sentences and reading time
get.description: Counts characters, words, unique words, sentences and paragraphs, and estimates reading (238 wpm) and speaking (150 wpm) time.

post.summary: MCP server (TextKit tools for AI agents)

Error.description: Error body. Errors raised by the API itself carry an `error` string. Errors raised by the RapidAPI gateway (missing or invalid key, not subscribed, quota or rate limit exceeded) carry a `message` string instead.

label.description: positive if compound >= 0.05, negative if <= -0.05, otherwise neutral.

compound.description: Normalised overall score from -1 (most negative) to +1 (most positive).

positive.description: Share of the text rated positive (0-1).

sentences.description: Per-sentence compound scores (up to 50 sentences, text cut to 300 chars). Null when the text is a single sentence.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code of the most likely language (zh-cn / zh-tw for Chinese).

candidates.description: Up to 5 candidate languages, most likely first.

flesch_reading_ease.description: Flesch Reading Ease (higher is easier; 60-70 is plain English).

level.description: Plain-English band for the Flesch score.

consensus_grade.description: Median of the five grade-level formulas.

complex_words.description: Words with three or more syllables.

reading_time_seconds.description: Estimated silent reading time at 238 words per minute.

keywords.description: Top single-word keywords (stop words and words of 2 letters or fewer removed), best first.

score.description: Relevance: frequency share weighted by word length.

phrases.description: Most frequent 2-4 word phrases between stop words.

contains_profanity.description: True if any profane word was found.

count.description: Number of profane words found (with repeats).

censored.description: Input with each profane word replaced by the mask character, letter for letter.

summary.description: Highest-scoring sentences joined in their original order.

original_sentences.description: Sentences considered in the input (omitted when the text already had no more sentences than requested).

language.description: Null if the language could not be detected.

readability.description: Null if the text has no words.

Forbidden.description: Forbidden: the request did not arrive through the RapidAPI gateway, or your RapidAPI key is not subscribed to this API.

example.message: You are not subscribed to this API.

ValidationError.description: Unprocessable: a required parameter is missing or a value is invalid. The `error` text says which.

example.error: A required parameter is missing or invalid

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests: your RapidAPI plan's rate limit or monthly quota was exceeded. Back off and retry, or upgrade your plan.

example.message: You have exceeded the rate limit per second for your plan, BASIC, by the API provider
